program_level.business_purpose: This appears to be a risk management and BWC (Bureau of Workers' Compensation) representative processing program. It handles risk experience records and processes representative relationships, likely for insurance or workers' compensation claims.
program_level.data_flows: The program processes risk numbers (WK-RKRSNBR) and manages multiple record types through various file operations. It reads from multiple source files (CMLHCL00, UTLMTB00, CMLMRP00) and writes to a target file (ADPWNP00). The program appears to handle both random and sequential access patterns, suggesting complex data retrieval and update logic.
business_rules: Addition of new BWC representative relationships (22000-ADD-BWC-REP)
Risk status validation through multiple status flags (SI-RISK-STAT, RISK-EXPERIENCE-STAT)
Sequential processing of related records with specific ordering (indicated by multiple START operations)
dependencies: CMLHCL00 - Likely a client/risk master file
UTLMTB00 - Appears to be a utility/lookup table
CMLMRP00 - Possibly a representative master file
ADPWNP00 - Output file for processed records
program_level.complexity_reasoning: The program exhibits high complexity due to: 1) Multiple file interactions with both random and sequential access patterns, 2) Complex business logic around risk and representative management, 3) Multiple status checks and validation rules, 4) Numerous interdependent processes and file operations, 5) Mix of numeric and text data handling with redefines
program_level.recommendations: Consider breaking this into smaller microservices: 1) Representative Management Service, 2) Risk Validation Service, 3) Data Access Layer for file operations. Use JPA for data access, implement proper transaction management, and consider using Spring Batch for bulk processing operations. Implement robust error handling and logging. Consider implementing an event-driven architecture for better scalability.
